attributes.probed_form: AXIS 1, `u8 unused0[8];` re-inserted between `f32 mat[16];` and `f32 oldpos[3];`. AXIS 2, the same insert PLUS `u8 unused4[12];` -> `u8 unused4[4];` (the byte-conserving split the pad laws mandate). AXIS 3, entry reassociation, `Enemy* e = (Enemy*)(row + 3608);` -> `Enemy* e = (Enemy*)(row += 3608);` (`row` is provably dead after this line - it has exactly two occurrences in the function, its declaration and this use).
attributes.residual: NOTHING RETAINED; baseline restored at real 176, T905/O905, multiset 4t, frame 208 both, 18/19 slots. SLOT 19 IS NAMED: slotdiff reports TARGET-ONLY slot 104 / OURS-ONLY slot 96, each with 2 uses, and both uses are `addi rX,r1,N` - an address-taken array, which is `f32 mat[16]`, confirmed by regnorm's only two genuinely structural rows (0x0d00 and 0x0d0c, `T addi r3,r1,104` vs `O addi r3,r1,96`). THE MECHANISM, which is new and is why the pad axis cannot close it: the two sides have IDENTICAL byte layouts below mat (slots 32/36/40/48/52/56/60/68/72/76/84/88/92 agree exactly) and identical frames (208), and each side carries exactly 8 bytes that no named local occupies - but TARGET's 8 dead bytes sit BETWEEN oldpos (ends 96) and mat (starts 104), while OURS sit ABOVE mat (mat ends 160, save base 168). Axis 1 measured the decisive fact: inserting 8 named bytes between mat and oldpos placed mat at 104 and made EVERY named slot agree, but the frame grew 208 -> 216 and the save base 168 -> 176, because our 8 dead bytes are an INDEPENDENT compiler-temp region that persists above whatever named block exists. So the local area is 148 bytes on both sides, but target spends all 148 on named locals while ours spends 140 named + 8 on a temp region that target does not allocate. The residual is therefore NOT a declaration-order or padding defect - it is an extra 8-byte compiler temp, never touched through r1 (0 accesses in the slot map), that our source shape causes MWCC to reserve. It is not reachable by an FP-expression respelling either: the opcode multiset differs by only 4 tokens and contains no FP opcode difference at all, so the float/double arithmetic already matches target instruction-for-instruction. DO-NOT-RETRY, each measured this session: re-inserting the between-mat-and-oldpos pad alone (frame 216, real 186); the byte-conserving pad split (the floor is FIXED, so shrinking the bottom pad moved half/hitWorld/newc/oldc/oldpos AND mat down 8 together - real 300, 6T/6O exclusive); the entry reassociation via in-place `+=` (broke count parity to O906 and real 269, though it did improve the multiset 4t -> 3t - parity outranks). REMAINING, unchanged and each individually named: (1) the 8-byte temp region above the named block; (2) target-only addi @0x324; (3) target-only lwz @0x9c4, allocator-forced; (4) two ours-only fmr @0x830/@0xbe4, the move_logic10 coalesce mechanism. WEBFRANK: NOT eligible - the multiset differs (target +1 addi +1 lwz vs ours -2 fmr), so no recolor rule can close it, and a stack displacement is not a recolor.
